children: and other memory stocks face a critical test as signs of cooling conventional memory pricing raise questions about how much further margins can expand. The concern comes ahead of Micron's Wednesday earnings report, with investors increasingly focused on whether strong AI demand can offset potentially weakening pricing across the broader DRAM market.

Micron is a leading manufacturer of DRAM, NAND flash and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), supplying chips used in smartphones, PCs, data centers and AI accelerators. Its profitability is highly sensitive to memory prices, production costs and industry supply-demand conditions.

Sara Awad of Tech Contrarians argues investors should pay closer attention to memory companies with limited HBM exposure, as their performance could reveal whether the broader pricing recovery is beginning to lose momentum.
Recent figures offer some warning signs.

WT Micro reported August sales growth of just 8%, while Nanya Technology's monthly revenue growth slowed sharply to 2% from 49% in July, despite reaching a record NT$44.7 billion. Macronix International also posted approximately 5% monthly growth, below July's pace.
Although revenue trends do not directly establish changes in selling prices, the moderation raises questions about conventional memory demand.
According to TrendForce estimates cited by Awad, DRAM average selling prices could increase
, substantially below the approximately 50% to 60% increase recorded in the second quarter.
Additional Chinese supply complicates the picture, with CXMT reportedly expected to reach roughly 20,000 wafer starts per month by year-end.
The critical number in Wednesday's earnings report will be gross-margin guidance.
Micron previously guided for an 86% gross margin after reporting 84.6%, leaving unusually high expectations embedded in the profitability outlook.
Investors should examine management's commentary on non-HBM pricing, conventional DRAM demand and HBM profitability.

A further margin increase would support the argument that supply discipline and pricing remain favorable. Conversely, flat or declining guidance could challenge expectations that memory profitability will continue expanding, particularly if PC and smartphone demand weakens while additional Chinese capacity enters the market.

title: Micron Stock Flashes New Warning Sign Before Earnings
